WHAT I VERIFIED MYSELF (Appendix A, probe P22; scripts in the scratchpad probe22/): (1) FRONTEND-DEV I1: in headless Chrome 154 with the U3 flags a page with a requestAnimationFrame loop got raf=0 in 6,000 ms of a 2 s interval that ran 3 times; the U3 recipe on the real page and real server code passed 8 of 8 runs (data-drawn="5"), and on a copy of public/ without the draw-at-the-tick line condition 4 failed in 6 of 8 runs (data-drawn="0" four times, no attribute twice) - so the sentence is needed and the tick is what makes step U3 meaningful. issues.severity: LOW (edge case; REQ-007 criterion 3 only for a role literally named main)
issues.title: A role literally named "main" gets no desk, but the routes of its tasks are attributed to the main session
issues.where: tools/src/pixel-office/public/office-model.js, buildOffice: deskIndexOf(key) returns the main session's desk for key "main" whenever the main session exists
issues.what: FRONTEND-DEV I3 reserves the key "main" so that such a role cannot take desk 0 or duplicate a character; that holds for desks, characters and the legend. Routes are different: with a role named main, a handoff launched by role alpha gets walker=alpha target=main (it walks to the MAIN SESSION's desk) and the result route gets walker=main target=alpha (the main session's character walks when that role's task stops). The design (section 3.6, OF-22) therefore says nothing about routes of such a role; I did not write the code's behaviour into the design.
issues.evidence: probe <вне проекта>/po-design/probe22/main-role.mjs (a journal in which alpha launches a role named main): characters main(desk 0), alpha(desk 1); legend alpha seated, main not seated; routes 3:handoff walker=main target=alpha; 5:handoff walker=alpha target=main; 6:result walker=main target=alpha
issues.proposal: REVIEWER to rule: (a) accept as a documented limitation (real roles are never named main), or (b) FRONTEND-DEV skips routes whose launcher or target is a role named main (one condition in buildOffice) and OF-22 then also checks 'no routes'. I would take (b); it changes no contract.

issues.title: ensureStateDir narrows the state directory's mode by chmod on the path after lstat (deliberate exception to 'by descriptor')
issues.what: Section 7.2 T15 records the code's behaviour: files are opened without following links and changed through the descriptor, but the directory's own 0700 narrowing is chmod on the path after lstat says 'plain directory, own uid'. A swap between lstat and chmod needs write access to the parent directory, i.e. the owner or an owner-level process, the same precondition as F3. The security re-check was asked to judge it; I did not rule and did not call it safe in the design.
issues.proposal: none from me; if SECURITY-REVIEWER or REVIEWER rejects the exception, one clause of T15 changes.

issues.severity: INFO (design text versus a source text)
issues.title: The security review's B1 test trigger no longer reaches EPIPE after F1
issues.what: The reviewer's B1 test (1) provokes the warning with a 300-character name. After F1 that request is a 404 and writes nothing to stderr, so used alone it would pass even without the B1 fix. SV-46 keeps the request and adds triggers that remain (a corrupt journal line read by GET /api/events?after=0, a failed append); section 10.1 says so. Checked by hand (design Appendix A, P22, third command): fixed code alive, copy without the stdout/stderr error listeners dead.
